summary: Head-of-line queueing and GPU contention in dedicated pool causing intermittent tail-latency spikes and timeouts
description: Issue summary: Since 2026-03-08 01:20 UTC, LuminaAI's dedicated GPU pool in us-west experienced repeated tail-latency spikes (5–10x typical) and intermittent request timeouts (up to 30s) for generation requests. Impact: Customer-facing inference endpoints reported 5–8% user-facing errors and elevated p99 latency causing degraded UX in production. Environment: Dedicated pool (luminaai-prod-usw-1), model pins: llama-2-70b-q4 and redwood-rlhf-13b, region us-west, hosted on p4d-equivalent instances. Steps to reproduce: 1) Send steady stream of mixed-length generation requests (avg tokens 120) at 200 qps to customer's pinned route; 2) Observe queue depth and latency distribution in Grafana; 3) During incidents observe long tail latencies and occasional 504s. Observed behavior: Tail latency spikes correlated with sudden host-level GPU compute/memory saturation on 1–2 nodes; other nodes in the pool remained underutilized. NVML showed high kernel run queue and frequent context switches. Autoscaler logs show rapid scale-down followed by delayed scale-up for short bursts. Temporary mitigations applied: increased pool min-replicas from 2 to 6, temporarily isolated the pool from batch-heavy tenant, and advised customer to pin to a higher-throughput route. Ask: Root-cause analysis and permanent remediation to avoid recurrence, plus a short postmortem and customer-facing summary.
steps_to_reproduce: Run mixed-length generation load (avg 120 tokens) at ~200 qps against customer's pinned endpoint
Monitor Grafana dashboard 'dedicated-pool/us-west/luminaai-prod-1' for GPU SM utilization and queue depth
Observe tail-latency p95/p99 and check autoscaler activity in the same window
logs_and_evidence: Scheduler events: eventIDs [sched-7791, sched-7792] showing preemption of small pods for a long-running batched job
investigation_notes: 03/08 02:00 UTC - SRE Diego: initial triage shows two nodes with >95% GPU SM util and memory usage while remaining nodes are <40% util; observed high kernel run queue length via NVML

03/08 03:10 UTC - SRE: found long-running batched jobs from another customer colocated on same nodes; those jobs hold CUDA contexts and sustain high SM usage, causing head-of-line blocking for short latency requests (noisy neighbor)

03/08 04:20 UTC - Observed autoscaler behaviour: scale-down aggressiveness (scaleDownDelay=60s) caused nodes to be removed too soon; short bursts then triggered slow scale-up due to conservative cooldown and scaleUpPolicy thresholds

03/08 05:00 UTC - Scheduler logs show preemption events and expensive kernel context switches when new lightweight containers try to run; GPU memory fragmentation observed (failed allocations logged) forcing some requests to queue and eventually time out
03/09 09:00 UTC - Reproduced locally by launching a persistent large-batch job on shared node while driving latency-sensitive traffic; reproduced p99 spikes and 504s

resolution: Short-term: Isolated LuminaAI pool by node-affinity and increased min-replicas to 6 to prevent head-of-line queueing; preemptively evicted colocated large-batch jobs from affected nodes and worked with owner to reschedule. Adjusted autoscaler config: increased scaleUpRate, removed aggressive scaleDown cooldown for dedicated pools, and set a 4-minute stabilization window for short bursts. Deployed a scheduler patch to prefer node-local placement for dedicated pools to reduce cross-tenant contention (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4321). Long-term: Implement GPU-aware bin-packing, enable MIG or cgroup GPU partitioning for eligible instance types, add autoscaler policy option 'dedicatedPoolStableMin' to avoid undershoot for production tenants, and update the Dedicated GPU isolation runbook. Customer remediation: LuminaAI was advised and verified that errors returned to normal after isolation. Incident closed after 48h of stable metrics.
